Introduction: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity
and myoclonus (PERM) is a severe form of stiff-person
spectrum disorder that can be associated with antibodies
against surface antigens (glycine receptor [GlyR] or
dipeptidyl-peptidase-like protein 6), and antibodies
inst intracellular antigens (glutamic acid decarboxyl-
[GAD65] or amphiphysin)..
‘Objectives: To report a clinical case and postmortem neu-
ropathological findings of a patient with PERM with
GilyR and GAD65 antibodies.
Patients and Methods: A 74-year-old man presented with
myoclonus and pain of the lower extremities. Despite ther-
